title: Partially Interpretable Decision Trees
abstract: arXiv:2611.06428v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Partially interpretable models extend simple interpretable models with the option to defer complicated inputs to an accurate but uninterpretable black-box model. By deferring more inputs, the model gets more accurate; by deferring fewer, it gets more interpretable. Existing procedures to train such partially interpretable models build on linear models or decision rules. We propose three algorithms for decision trees: a partially interpretable extension of the existing Branches algorithm, which performs exact search to optimize the tree; a conversion algorithm that we run on top of standard CART, which is computationally more efficient; and a generalized CART whose splitting criterion takes into account the option to defer while growing the tree. translated_abstract: 部分可解释模型在简单可解释模型的基础上进行扩展，增加了将复杂输入转交给准确但不可解释的黑箱模型处理的选项。转交的输入越多，模型越准确；转交的越少，模型越可解释。现有的训练此类部分可解释模型的方法大多基于线性模型或决策规则。我们提出了三种决策树算法：一是现有Branches算法的部分可解释扩展，该算法通过精确搜索来优化树结构；二是在标准CART之上运行的转换算法，其计算效率更高；三是广义CART算法，其分裂准则在树的生长过程中考虑了转交选项。令人惊讶的是，这三种算法在许多真实数据集上的表现相似。我们可以通过对智能树构建潜在收益的形式化界限来解释这一现象。
tldr: 该论文提出了三种部分可解释决策树算法（Branches精确搜索扩展、基于CART的转换算法和考虑转交选项的广义CART），并通过形式化界限证明它们在真实数据集上表现相似的原因在于智能树构建的潜在收益本身有限。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes three partially interpretable decision tree algorithms (an exact-search Branches extension, a CART-based conversion algorithm, and a generalized CART with defer-aware splitting) and explains their similar performance across real-world datasets via a formal bound on the potential gain of smart tree construction.
